brief.goal: Design a randomised experiment that shows whether an onboarding checklist increases week-1 retention of the note-taking app.
brief.audience: The product and data leads who decide whether to ship the checklist.
brief.assumptions: Week-1 retention is about 30% today. The checklist is built and behind a feature flag. Enough new users sign up each week to fill both groups within a few weeks ([WEEKLY SIGN-UPS]).
brief.outOfScope: Redesigning the onboarding screens; changes to paid acquisition.
brief.doneWhen: All 7 reviewed sections are approved by the Critic, and anything unresolved is listed under Open questions.

sections.name: Hypothesis
sections.guidance: One testable hypothesis with a direction and a null hypothesis.
content: H1: New users who see the onboarding checklist have higher week-1 retention than new users who don't.
H0: Week-1 retention is the same with and without the checklist.
Expected direction: an increase from about 30% to 36% (a 6-point lift), tested two-sided.

sections.name: Variables
sections.guidance: Independent, dependent and controlled variables, each with how it is operationalised.
content: Independent: onboarding checklist shown (treatment) or not shown (control), set by the feature flag at first launch.
Dependent: week-1 retention = the user opens the app on any day 2–7 after sign-up (from the analytics events table).
Controlled: app version, sign-up platform and acquisition channel are recorded and balanced by randomisation.
sources: Data analyst's answer: measuring week-1 retention

sections.name: Method
sections.guidance: Design (e.g. randomised A/B, within-subjects), procedure step by step, duration.
content: Design: randomised A/B test, between-subjects, 1:1 allocation at first launch.
Procedure: the flag service assigns each new account; treatment sees the 5-step checklist on the home screen until it is completed or dismissed.
Duration: enrol until both groups are full, then follow each user for 7 days; no change to the app during the test.
Participants who see the checklist can dismiss it at any time, as the Ethics reviewer asked.
sources: Ethics reviewer's answer: hiding the checklist from the control group

sections.name: Sample and controls
sections.guidance: Who takes part, how they are recruited and assigned, the control condition, and the sample size with its justification.
content: Participants: every new sign-up on iOS and Android during the test; existing users and staff accounts are excluded.
Assignment: the flag service randomises each new account 1:1 at first launch, keyed on the account ID, so a reinstall keeps the same group.
Control: the current onboarding with no checklist and no other change.
Sample size: 961 per group, 1922 in total: enough to detect a rise from 30% to 36% at α 0.05 with 80% power (sample-size calculator).
sources: Sample size: 961 per group, 1,922 total (two proportions, 30% vs 36%, α 0.05, power 0.80)

reviews.note: Assignment isn't described: say how new users are randomised and what happens to users who reinstall. The control condition is named but not defined.
before: Participants: new sign-ups on iOS and Android during the test.
Sample size: 961 per group (1922 in total), from the Data analyst's calculation.

sections.name: Measurements
sections.guidance: Each metric with its exact definition, unit, time window and data source.
content: Primary: week-1 retention (yes/no) = at least one app open on days 2–7 after sign-up, from the analytics events table, in each user's local time.
Secondary: checklist completion rate (treatment only), notes created in week 1 (count).
Guardrail: uninstalls in week 1 (count), to catch a checklist that annoys users.

sections.name: Analysis plan
sections.guidance: Primary test, significance level, power, how missing data and multiple comparisons are handled, and the decision rule.
content: Primary test: two-sided two-proportion z-test on week-1 retention, α 0.05, power 0.80.
Analyse when both groups reach 961 users with 7 days of follow-up; no peeking before that.
Missing data: users with no events after day 1 count as not retained; accounts deleted in week 1 are excluded and reported.
Secondary metrics are reported with Holm-corrected p-values and do not decide the outcome.
Decision rule: ship the checklist if retention is significantly higher and the uninstall rate is not higher.
sources: Sample size: 961 per group, 1,922 total (two proportions, 30% vs 36%, α 0.05, power 0.80)

sections.name: Risks and ethics
sections.guidance: Consent, privacy and data retention, possible harms and how they are mitigated, and stop conditions.
content: Consent: covered by the app's terms for product improvement tests; no extra data is collected for the test.
Privacy: only account IDs and event counts are analysed; the analysis table is deleted 90 days after the decision.
Harm: low; the checklist can be dismissed. Stop the test if week-1 uninstalls in treatment exceed control by 2 points.
Participants with accessibility settings on get the same checklist with screen-reader labels.

sections.name: Open questions
sections.guidance: Questions raised during the run that no agent could answer. Not reviewed.
content: How many new users sign up per week, so we know how long enrolment takes? (raised by Methods specialist)
Should users who dismiss the checklist on day 1 be analysed separately? (raised by Data analyst)
